title: Many analysts, one dataset — red cards and skin tone
question: Are soccer players with darker skin tone more likely to be given a red card by referees?

ai.label: agentic runs
ai._discover_note: A run counts only with both artifacts, and a report under 400 bytes is a stub rather than a write-up. These were hardcoded in distill.py until they moved here; the values are unchanged.

human.label: human teams
human._discover_note: Code is OPTIONAL here -- 12 of 31 teams deposited no script, and they still count as runs that contribute zero decisions, which is the study's largest caveat. A list under a role means candidates: the largest present becomes the role, the next becomes <role>_secondary. survey and report are two prose channels at two time points.
human.note: 12 of 31 teams deposited no script and contribute zero decisions

context._comment: Domain context, appended to prompts as DATA. It never edits prompt text, so prompt_hash is identical across studies and the shared-instrument claim is checkable. See templates/intake.md section C.
context.dataset: One row per player-referee dyad, European leagues 2012-13.

glossary.dyad: one player-referee pair; rows are dyads, not matches or players
glossary.redCards: count over all games in that dyad
glossary.games: appearances in the dyad; the natural exposure offset
glossary.IAT, Exp: implicit and explicit bias scores for the referee's country

not_decisions: loading the CSV from a fixed path
easily_missed_decisions: combining the two skin-tone raters into one exposure
the reference date age is computed from
which columns survive into the modelling frame
whether dyads with zero games are dropped

research_questions: Is the garden of forking paths a real, mappable object, and what shape is it?
Where do analysts agree, and where is disagreement concentrated?
Do fork choices predict the reported conclusion out of sample?
Does the assigned brief change what analysts do, or only what they report?
How much of what is done is never written down?

predictions._comment: Recorded before results where possible, so a later match is a prediction rather than a story. Reconstructed here; binding in a new study.
predictions.outcome: all three are contested; the fork choices DO predict the reported conclusion out of sample (verdict cross-validated R2 0.26, z 0.25). CORRECTED 2026-08-30: the earlier claim that none predicts out of sample was an artifact of a cross-validation bug -- per-fold design matrices were aligned by column position rather than identity, misaligning 41-48 of ~50 columns in all five folds. See report, Shapley attribution.

outcomes.note: no generator in this package; 52 of 207 records have no provenance. See data/outcomes/README.md

provenance._comment: Every run carries one of these. Provenance stratifies, it does not filter -- every run counts toward the statistics, and stability.py reports them with and without non-corpus runs so any drift is visible.
provenance.corpus: extracted from an analysis a real analyst wrote
provenance.itinerary: assembled from options the corpus already contains
provenance.authored: contains an operation no run in the corpus performed

unfair.why: no human outcomes; 19 of 31 teams code-backed; different brief
